quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Rafael volunteers at the hospital radio station on Thursday evenings. He plays requests from patients, reads short stories aloud and announces the weather for the week. Nurses say the programme helps people who cannot sleep feel less alone. Last month, one ward sent a thank-you card signed by every patient.
options: Nurses ask Rafael to announce the weather for the hospital staff.
Rafael reads short stories to sleepless patients on most nights of the week.
Rafael's radio programme brings comfort to hospital patients.
Hospital radio stations are more popular than television in wards.
quests.correctAnswer: Rafael's radio programme brings comfort to hospital patients.
quests.hint: Decide what all the details prove together, then reject options that only echo one detail.
quests.explanation: Requests, stories and the ward's card all point to the same effect: the programme comforts patients. Reading stories nightly changes the schedule, and the other options add comparisons or duties that are not mentioned.
keyPoints: Rafael presents a weekly radio show at a hospital.
He plays requests, reads stories and gives the weather.
Nurses and patients value it for easing loneliness.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The tool library on Mill Road lends drills, ladders and paint sprayers for a small yearly fee. Most people need such equipment only once or twice a year, so buying it seems wasteful. Members save money, and garages and sheds stay less crowded. The library also runs Saturday workshops where neighbours learn basic repairs from experienced members.
options: Saturday workshops are the library's main source of income.
Buying tools tends to be cheaper than borrowing them, since members pay a yearly fee.
Members pay a yearly fee for garage and shed space.
A tool library lets neighbours share equipment and learn skills.
quests.correctAnswer: A tool library lets neighbours share equipment and learn skills.
quests.hint: Look for the option that covers both the lending and the workshops.
quests.explanation: The paragraph gives the reason for sharing tools and adds a second service, repair workshops. Options about fees, all-purchase waste or income narrow or distort what is said.
keyPoints: The tool library lends equipment for a small annual fee.
Sharing saves money and space because tools are rarely used.
Saturday workshops teach basic repair skills.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Night buses in the city used to run only until midnight, so shift workers often walked home in the dark. After a survey of hospital and restaurant staff, the council added three late routes. Ridership has been higher than expected, and the number of taxi complaints has fallen. The council is now studying whether to add weekend services too.
options: The council has already extended the late routes to weekends after an early trial.
Late buses were added so workers could get home safely.
A survey found that hospital staff prefer walking home.
Taxi companies have complained about the new bus routes.
quests.correctAnswer: Late buses were added so workers could get home safely.
quests.hint: Find the reason for the change, the change itself and what it led to.
quests.explanation: A survey showed workers needed transport, the council added routes, and results were positive. Wrong options reverse taxi complaints, treat a study as completed, or reverse the survey findings.
keyPoints: Night buses once stopped at midnight, leaving shift workers to walk.
The council added three late routes after surveying staff.
Ridership is high, and weekend services are being studied.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Kwabena started as an electrician's apprentice at seventeen. For two years, he carried cables, watched carefully and asked questions at lunch. Now he wires small houses on his own and trains new apprentices himself. He says the best lesson was that slow, careful work saves more time than fast work that must be redone.
options: Kwabena believes fast work often saves more time than careful work.
Kwabena carried cables for two years before he was allowed to watch.
Kwabena's careful apprenticeship turned him into a skilled, independent electrician.
New apprentices now carry cables for Kwabena at lunchtime.
quests.correctAnswer: Kwabena's careful apprenticeship turned him into a skilled, independent electrician.
quests.hint: Track how the person changes from the start to the end.
quests.explanation: The paragraph moves from apprentice to trainer and ends with the value of careful work. Wrong options contradict that lesson, reverse the order of learning or invent a lunchtime duty.
keyPoints: Kwabena began as an apprentice electrician at seventeen.
He learned by watching and asking questions for two years.
He now works independently and trains others.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Every spring, Mrs. Lindqvist's class grows vegetables in the school garden. Together the children measure the seedlings, record the rainfall and compare which soil works best. In summer, the cook uses the harvest in school lunches. Parents say their children now happily try foods they used to refuse at home.
options: Children refuse vegetables because they measure the seedlings.
A school garden teaches children science and encourages healthy eating.
The school cook grows most of the vegetables that are used in the lunches.
Rainfall records are the most important part of the garden.
quests.correctAnswer: A school garden teaches children science and encourages healthy eating.
quests.hint: Combine what the children do in the garden with what happens afterwards.
quests.explanation: Growing, measuring and cooking connect classroom learning with what children eat. Wrong options exaggerate the cook's role, reverse the effect on eating or promote a single activity.
keyPoints: Mrs. Lindqvist's class grows vegetables each spring.
Children measure, record and compare as part of learning.
Harvested food goes into school lunches, and pupils try new foods.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A local seed library lets gardeners borrow packets in spring and return seeds from their best plants in autumn. Members share tips on the noticeboard, and rare varieties that supermarkets rarely sell are kept alive. The library asks for no money, only that borrowers bring something back. Volunteers say the system builds trust as well as gardens.
options: The noticeboard is the library's main way to store seeds.
Borrowers must pay money for each packet they take.
Supermarkets sell most of the seeds that gardeners return.
A seed library keeps rare plants alive by sharing.
quests.correctAnswer: A seed library keeps rare plants alive by sharing.
quests.hint: Ask what makes the system work and what it achieves.
quests.explanation: Borrowing and returning seeds preserves varieties and builds trust among members. Wrong options bring in supermarkets, say money is required or make a small feature the main point.
keyPoints: Gardeners borrow seeds in spring and return seeds in autumn.
The system keeps rare varieties available and allows tip-sharing.
No payment is needed, and volunteers say trust grows.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The supermarket on Church Lane now holds a quiet hour every Tuesday morning. Lights are dimmed, music is switched off and the checkout beeps are turned down. The change was requested by families of children who find noise stressful. Other shoppers have also said they enjoy the calmer atmosphere, and the store plans to add a second hour.
options: A quiet hour helps noise-sensitive shoppers, and others like it.
Children are the main customers who benefit from quiet hours, while other shoppers dislike them.
The supermarket plans to close for one hour each morning to restock shelves.
Music and checkout beeps have been switched off for good in the store.
quests.correctAnswer: A quiet hour helps noise-sensitive shoppers, and others like it.
quests.hint: Check whether an option turns a limited change into a permanent one.
quests.explanation: The store made a weekly change for people sensitive to noise and found it popular more widely. Wrong options extend the change to all times, restrict its benefits or swap 'hour' with 'closing'.
keyPoints: The supermarket holds a quiet hour on Tuesday mornings.
Lights, music and beeps are reduced.
It began for families of noise-sensitive children but others like it, so a second hour is planned.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When Sipho's dog disappeared, he printed fifty posters and put them up around the neighbourhood. A boy who saw one remembered a dog outside the bakery. Sipho arrived within minutes and found his dog sitting patiently by the door. Afterwards, he added a note to every poster saying the dog was home and thanking everyone.
options: Sipho printed fifty posters because he had lost many pets.
Sipho found his dog after a bakery employee brought it home.
The boy who saw a poster kept the dog for a week.
Sipho found his lost dog thanks to posters and a neighbour's tip.
quests.correctAnswer: Sipho found his lost dog thanks to posters and a neighbour's tip.
quests.hint: Look at the chain of events that leads to the dog's return.
quests.explanation: The posters led to a sighting, the sighting led to the reunion, and the note completed the story. Wrong options change who found the dog or invent events.
keyPoints: Sipho's dog disappeared, so he put up fifty posters.
A boy who saw a poster remembered the dog near the bakery.
Sipho recovered his dog and thanked the neighbourhood.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The town's welcome signs are now in three languages: English, Arabic and Polish. The council made the change after a study showed that a fifth of residents speak one of the latter two at home. Shop owners have added translated menus and price lists as well. Some older residents worried about cost, but the signs were paid for by a small grant.
options: Shop owners were told to translate their menus by law.
Multilingual signs reflect the languages spoken by the town's residents.
Most residents now speak Arabic or Polish at home, according to the study.
Older residents refused to pay for the new signs.
quests.correctAnswer: Multilingual signs reflect the languages spoken by the town's residents.
quests.hint: Which option keeps the reason for the change and the response to it?
quests.explanation: The signs follow the town's language mix, and shops joined in voluntarily. Wrong options exaggerate the numbers, claim residents paid, or say the shops were forced.
keyPoints: The town's signs now appear in English, Arabic and Polish.
A study showed many residents speak Arabic or Polish at home.
A small grant paid for the signs, and shops added translations.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Minibus drivers in the district have started using a phone app to share traffic updates. When one driver reports a blocked road, others choose different routes before reaching it. Journeys that once took an hour now take about forty minutes. Passengers appreciate the shorter waits, though a few drivers say they miss chatting at the roadside.
options: The app reports traffic to passengers who pay a monthly subscription fee.
An app that shares traffic reports has made minibus journeys quicker.
Minibus drivers now spend an hour chatting at the roadside.
Passengers made the app to avoid blocked roads.
quests.correctAnswer: An app that shares traffic reports has made minibus journeys quicker.
quests.hint: Trace how one driver's report leads to a change for many.
quests.explanation: Shared reports let drivers avoid blockages, which shortens trips. Wrong options make a small regret the main result, change who created the app or add a fee.
keyPoints: Minibus drivers share road information through a phone app.
Others avoid blocked roads after reports come in.
Trips have shortened from an hour to about forty minutes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hye-jin failed her driving test twice because of nerves. Her instructor suggested practising the test route on quiet Sunday mornings until she knew every turn. She also began breathing slowly before each lesson. On her third attempt, she passed with only one minor mistake and thanked her instructor with a box of pastries.
options: Hye-jin passed her test on the second attempt with a perfect score.
Hye-jin failed her test twice because she did not know the route.
Hye-jin's instructor gave her pastries after the third test.
Hye-jin passed her test by practising and staying calm.
quests.correctAnswer: Hye-jin passed her test by practising and staying calm.
quests.hint: Match each problem to the action that responded to it.
quests.explanation: Nerves caused failures, so route practice and breathing were her response, leading to success. Wrong options invent a cause, reverse who gave the gift or ignore the minor mistake.
keyPoints: Hye-jin failed her driving test twice because she felt nervous.
She practised the route and used slow breathing.
She passed on the third try.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The bicycle co-op in the old warehouse charges nothing for repairs, but asks each visitor to help fix at least one other bike. Beginners learn to change tyres, while experienced members handle gears and brakes. By the end of the year, the co-op had repaired more than four hundred bicycles. Several regular visitors have since become volunteer instructors.
options: A bicycle co-op repairs bikes through shared work and teaches repair skills.
The co-op sold four hundred bicycles by the end of the year.
The co-op charges visitors a small fee for each repair.
Experienced members are the ones allowed to fix bicycles, while beginners watch.
quests.correctAnswer: A bicycle co-op repairs bikes through shared work and teaches repair skills.
quests.hint: See how the rule about helping others shapes everything in the paragraph.
quests.explanation: Repairs are free in exchange for helping, and learning spreads as visitors become instructors. Wrong options reverse the fee, restrict who repairs, or turn repairs into sales.
keyPoints: The co-op offers free repairs in return for helping someone else.
Beginners and experts each handle different tasks.
Over four hundred bicycles were repaired, and some visitors became instructors.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Once a month, a group of teenagers visits the Willow Court retirement home to play board games with residents. The teenagers began going for a school service project but kept returning after the project ended. Residents say they look forward to the visits all month, and the home's manager has noticed more conversation in the common room. Two teenagers now help with the gardening as well.
options: The home's manager organised the visits for teenagers' school marks.
Teen visits to a retirement home became a lasting habit.
Teenagers stopped visiting when their school project finished.
Residents at Willow Court are required to play board games.
quests.correctAnswer: Teen visits to a retirement home became a lasting habit.
quests.hint: Which option explains how the visits started and why they continued?
quests.explanation: A school project became a regular tradition that benefits both groups. Wrong options add a rule, reverse the timeline or invent a motive.
keyPoints: Teenagers play board games with residents once a month.
The visits began as a school project but continued.
Residents enjoy them, and some teenagers now help in the garden.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A coworking space near the station rents desks by the hour as well as by the month. Freelancers who work from cafés say they like having a quiet place with reliable internet. The space also hosts a weekly lunch where members swap advice. The owner says that the lunches produced two business partnerships within a year.
options: A coworking space gives freelancers both desks and community.
The weekly lunch is organised by two business partners.
Freelancers stopped using cafés because the space was cheaper.
The space charges monthly rent for desks and does not offer hourly rates.
quests.correctAnswer: A coworking space gives freelancers both desks and community.
quests.hint: Ask what the space offers besides desks.
quests.explanation: Desks, internet and lunches together create a workplace and a network. Wrong options invent a price comparison, reverse the rental rule or misplace who organises the lunch.
keyPoints: The coworking space rents desks by the hour or month.
Freelancers value the quiet and the reliable internet.
Weekly lunches have led to two business partnerships.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Electric scooters appeared in the city last summer, and complaints followed quickly. Riders left them on pavements, and older pedestrians tripped over them. The council responded by marking parking zones and fining riders who left scooters elsewhere. Complaints have fallen by half, although some residents say the zones are too few.
options: Complaints fell by half because the zones became more numerous.
Scooters have been banned from the city after last summer.
Parking zones and fines have reduced complaints about abandoned scooters.
Older pedestrians refuse to walk on pavements near scooters.
quests.correctAnswer: Parking zones and fines have reduced complaints about abandoned scooters.
quests.hint: Sort the paragraph into problem, response and remaining concern.
quests.explanation: Scooters caused pavement problems, the council created zones and fines, and complaints dropped, with a remaining concern. Wrong options invent a ban, exaggerate pedestrians' behaviour or reverse the cause of the improvement.
keyPoints: Scooters left on pavements caused complaints and accidents.
The council introduced parking zones and fines.
Complaints halved, but some say there are too few zones.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A farmers' market app lets shoppers order fruit and vegetables in the morning and collect them in the afternoon. Farmers can see how much to harvest, which reduces waste. Shoppers avoid long queues and get fresher produce. The app charges farmers a small fee, but most say the reduction in waste more than covers it.
options: The app charges shoppers a fee when they collect their orders.
Shoppers must harvest their produce before collecting it.
Farmers lose money because of the app's fee, which outweighs their savings.
A market app cuts waste and saves shoppers time.
quests.correctAnswer: A market app cuts waste and saves shoppers time.
quests.hint: Look for the benefit to farmers and the benefit to shoppers together.
quests.explanation: Advance orders help farmers harvest exactly what is needed and save shoppers time. Wrong options exaggerate the fee, misread who harvests or move the fee to shoppers.
keyPoints: The app allows morning orders and afternoon collection.
Farmers harvest to demand, reducing waste.
Shoppers avoid queues, and farmers say the benefits outweigh the small fee.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Doctors say teenagers need eight to ten hours of sleep, but many get much less. Phones kept in bedrooms are one cause, since notifications interrupt sleep. Some schools now ask students to leave phones in a locker overnight during exam weeks. Teachers report that students in the trial arrived more alert and made fewer careless mistakes.
options: Phone-free bedrooms may help teenagers sleep and concentrate.
Most teenagers already get ten hours of sleep each night.
Schools have banned phones from students' homes during exam weeks.
Teenagers sleep too little mainly because schools start lessons late in the day.
quests.correctAnswer: Phone-free bedrooms may help teenagers sleep and concentrate.
quests.hint: Check the words 'one cause' and 'trial' before choosing.
quests.explanation: Phones are described as one cause of poor sleep, and a school trial suggested benefits. Wrong options contradict the sleep problem, treat one cause as the only one or extend the trial to homes.
keyPoints: Teenagers need more sleep than many get.
Phones in bedrooms interrupt sleep.
A trial with lockers led to more alert students.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Before exams, many students study for hours without breaks and then feel exhausted. Psychologists suggest short breaks every forty minutes, including a walk or a glass of water. The breaks give the brain time to store what has been read. Students who follow this pattern often remember more, even though they study for slightly less time in total.
options: Students should study for hours without stopping before exams.
Students who take breaks tend to study for much longer in total.
Short breaks help students remember more from revision.
Psychologists say walking is more important than studying.
quests.correctAnswer: Short breaks help students remember more from revision.
quests.hint: Find the advice, then the reason the writer gives for it.
quests.explanation: The advice to take breaks is supported by the idea that the brain needs time to store information. Wrong options reverse the advice, exaggerate walking or say total time increases.
keyPoints: Many students study for hours and become exhausted.
Short breaks every forty minutes help the brain store information.
Students who take them remember more despite slightly less study time.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Volunteers at the community centre teach a weekend first aid course for free. Participants practise bandaging, learn what to do if someone is choking and watch a demonstration of the recovery position. Each person receives a small kit to take home. Last year, two graduates used what they learned to help people during a street accident.
options: The course is aimed at people who work at the community centre.
Participants pay for a kit before each course begins.
Two graduates taught the course after a street accident.
A free first aid course prepares residents to help in emergencies.
quests.correctAnswer: A free first aid course prepares residents to help in emergencies.
quests.hint: Ask what the course is for, and what evidence shows it works.
quests.explanation: The course teaches practical skills, and the street accident shows the skills being used. Wrong options add payment, reverse who taught whom, or narrow who can attend.
keyPoints: Volunteers offer a free weekend first aid course.
It covers bandaging, choking and the recovery position.
Graduates used the skills to help in a street accident.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The pharmacy on Dock Street has started delivering medicines to older customers who cannot easily leave home. Staff call each week to check what people need and to ask how they are feeling. Several families say the calls have made them feel less worried about relatives living alone. The pharmacist notes that a friendly voice sometimes matters as much as the medicine itself.
options: The pharmacy asks families to deliver medicines themselves.
A pharmacy supports older customers who live alone.
Older customers must leave home to collect their medicines.
The pharmacist believes medicine matters less than money.
quests.correctAnswer: A pharmacy supports older customers who live alone.
quests.hint: Include both the practical service and the personal contact.
quests.explanation: Deliveries meet a practical need, and calls give reassurance to customers and families. Wrong options reverse who delivers, contradict the purpose or distort the pharmacist's comment.
keyPoints: The pharmacy delivers medicines to older customers.
Staff phone weekly to ask what they need.
Families feel reassured, and the pharmacist values the friendly contact.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Rice farmers in the delta now receive text messages with the weather forecast for the next three days. When heavy rain is expected, they delay planting so seeds are not washed away. One farmer estimates that he saved nearly a quarter of his seed last season. The service is free, paid for by a group of local banks.
options: Text forecasts help rice farmers protect their seeds.
Farmers now plant during heavy rain to save time.
Local banks plant seeds on farmers' behalf during storms.
The forecast service costs farmers a quarter of their income.
quests.correctAnswer: Text forecasts help rice farmers protect their seeds.
quests.hint: Trace how the forecast changes what farmers do and what results.
quests.explanation: A warning about rain leads to delayed planting, which protects seeds. Wrong options change who plants, reverse the farmers' decision or invent a cost.
keyPoints: Farmers get free text messages with three-day forecasts.
They delay planting when heavy rain is expected.
One farmer saved nearly a quarter of his seed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The fishing village of Palo Verde limits each boat to a fixed catch per week. Fishers first resisted the rule, but fish numbers have begun to recover after three seasons. Younger fishers say the limit lets them plan and earn more steadily. A few older fishers still argue that the quota is too strict.
options: Younger fishers oppose limits on their boats' weekly catches.
Fish numbers have returned to their old level after three seasons, according to fishers.
Fishers in Palo Verde now support the quota, including the older ones.
Catch limits are restoring fish numbers, but opinions differ.
quests.correctAnswer: Catch limits are restoring fish numbers, but opinions differ.
quests.hint: Find the result and the qualification the writer adds.
quests.explanation: The quota is working for the fish and for younger fishers, but a few disagree. Wrong options reverse the opinions or exaggerate the recovery.
keyPoints: Palo Verde limits each boat's weekly catch.
Fish numbers are starting to recover after three seasons.
Younger fishers favour it; some older ones say it is too strict.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A textile recycling project collects worn clothes and cuts them into strips for weaving. Local women then make rugs and bags from the strips and sell them at a weekend stall. The project keeps clothing out of landfill and gives the weavers a small income. Customers like that each item is different.
options: Local women buy new clothes to make into rugs.
Old clothes become rugs and bags, creating income.
Customers dislike that the items look different from each other.
The stall is open on weekdays and closes at weekends.
quests.correctAnswer: Old clothes become rugs and bags, creating income.
quests.hint: Ask what is made, who benefits and what problem is reduced.
quests.explanation: The project turns waste into products that earn money. Wrong options reverse the source of the material, expand the stall's opening times or contradict customers' opinions.
keyPoints: Worn clothes are collected and cut into strips.
Local women weave rugs and bags to sell at a stall.
This reduces landfill waste and provides a small income.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When a storm cut the power in Ashford for three days, the community hall became an unofficial hub. Volunteers cooked hot meals on gas stoves, and residents charged phones from a borrowed generator. Teenagers checked on elderly neighbours door to door. When the lights returned, the mayor thanked the volunteers, and the hall committee is now planning an emergency stock of supplies.
options: Elderly neighbours cooked hot meals at the community hall.
The hall committee has stopped planning after the power returned.
A blackout brought neighbours together and prompted emergency planning.
The mayor's team provided the meals during the blackout.
quests.correctAnswer: A blackout brought neighbours together and prompted emergency planning.
quests.hint: Look for the event, the community response and what it led to.
quests.explanation: The blackout produced a coordinated community effort and inspired preparation. Wrong options misattribute the meals or roles or say planning ended.
keyPoints: A storm cut Ashford's power for three days.
The community hall provided meals, phone charging and checks on elderly neighbours.
The committee now plans an emergency supply stock.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A village in the highlands had trouble storing water for the dry months. Residents built stone tanks beside the school, fed by pipes from the roofs. In the wet season, the tanks fill in a few weeks, and the water lasts until autumn. Pupils learn to check the tanks and keep records, which the teacher says is better than any textbook.
options: The tanks fill during the dry months and last through winter.
Stone tanks give a highland village dry-season water.
The school teaches pupils to build stone tanks for other villages.
Textbooks are better than learning to check the tanks.
quests.correctAnswer: Stone tanks give a highland village dry-season water.
quests.hint: Match the problem with the solution and the extra benefit.
quests.explanation: Tanks solve the dry-season shortage, and pupils gain practical experience. Wrong options change the tanks' purpose, reverse the season or misquote the teacher.
keyPoints: The village struggled to store water for dry months.
Residents built roof-fed stone tanks by the school.
Pupils help by checking the tanks and keeping records.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A primary school introduced a rule that lunch must be eaten seated and unhurried for at least twenty minutes. The cook noticed that less food went into the bins. Teachers found that afternoon lessons started more calmly. Some children complained at first, but most now say lunchtime is their favourite part of the day.
options: Unhurried lunches reduced waste and calmed lessons.
Children were asked to leave their lunches half-eaten.
Teachers introduced the rule to shorten lessons.
Most children still complain about the twenty minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Unhurried lunches reduced waste and calmed lessons.
quests.hint: Which option connects the rule with its effects?
quests.explanation: The rule slowed lunch, which led to less waste and calmer lessons. Wrong options reverse the effect on food, invent a motive or claim most children still object.
keyPoints: Children must sit and take at least twenty minutes for lunch.
Less food is thrown away, and afternoons begin more calmly.
Initial complaints have turned into approval.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: After-school tutoring at the library is run by university students who volunteer once a week. Each tutor works with the same child for a term, so trust builds gradually. Teachers say the children's confidence has grown as much as their marks. The scheme now has a waiting list, and the library is looking for more volunteers.
options: The library has stopped accepting new volunteers because the waiting list is long.
Teachers believe marks matter more than children's confidence.
Volunteer tutoring builds children's confidence and marks.
Children choose a new tutor each week during the term.
quests.correctAnswer: Volunteer tutoring builds children's confidence and marks.
quests.hint: Check the details about time and demand carefully.
quests.explanation: Long-term pairing builds trust, results are positive, and demand is high. Wrong options reverse the arrangement, contradict the recruitment need or distort teachers' views.
keyPoints: University students tutor children at the library each week.
Each tutor keeps the same child for a term.
Confidence and marks improve, and a waiting list has formed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Old bridges in the region are being inspected by drones instead of climbing crews. The drones photograph cracks in places that used to take hours to reach. Engineers say inspections are now safer and about twice as fast. However, they add that drones cannot tap concrete to hear hollow spots, so people still check the most critical areas.
options: Drones speed up bridge checks and cannot replace people.
Inspections take twice as long because drones fly slowly.
Climbing crews prefer drones because they hear hollow spots.
Drones now replace human inspectors on the most critical bridge areas.
quests.correctAnswer: Drones speed up bridge checks and cannot replace people.
quests.hint: Include the limit the engineers mention at the end.
quests.explanation: The paragraph gives advantages of drones and a qualification that people still inspect key areas. Wrong options remove humans, reverse the tapping ability or reverse speed.
keyPoints: Drones photograph cracks on old bridges.
This makes inspections safer and about twice as fast.
People still check critical areas because drones cannot tap concrete.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ms. Abara's bakery has two ovens: a large one that heats slowly and a small one that heats quickly. She uses the large oven for bread, which needs steady heat for an hour. The small one bakes cookies and rolls in minutes. Customers know that morning loaves are ready by eight, but cookies keep coming all afternoon.
options: Cookies are ready by eight, though bread keeps coming through the afternoon.
Ms. Abara has a single oven that she uses for bread and cookies.
The small oven is used for bread because it heats faster.
Two ovens suit different baked goods and timings.
quests.correctAnswer: Two ovens suit different baked goods and timings.
quests.hint: Keep each oven attached to what it bakes and when.
quests.explanation: Each oven has its own strength, and together they explain the timing of products. Wrong options swap the ovens or the schedule or reduce them to one.
keyPoints: Ms. Abara has a large slow oven and a small quick oven.
The large one bakes morning bread, and the small one bakes cookies and rolls.
Bread is ready by eight, and cookies come out through the afternoon.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The Grand Palm hotel kept losing guests to cheaper rivals, so the manager asked former guests why they had left. Many said the rooms were fine but the breakfast was disappointing. The hotel hired a local baker and began serving regional dishes. Reviews improved within months, and the restaurant now attracts visitors who are not even staying overnight.
options: Former guests said the rooms were the reason they left.
Listening to complaints helped a hotel win guests back.
The local baker now runs the hotel's restaurant.
The hotel cut its room prices to compete with cheaper rivals.
quests.correctAnswer: Listening to complaints helped a hotel win guests back.
quests.hint: Find the problem, the way it was investigated and what the hotel changed.
quests.explanation: The manager identified the real complaint, breakfast, and fixed it, which improved reviews and brought in extra customers. Wrong options replace the cause with price or rooms or invent a change in ownership.
keyPoints: The hotel was losing guests to cheaper rivals.
Former guests said the breakfast, not the rooms, disappointed them.
A local baker and regional dishes improved reviews and attracted outside diners.
